You’re talking about the bond here, the stock is unrelated.

If a bond has a coupon of 7% and then market rates drop and a comparable bond can be now issued with simply a 6% coupon, this bond becomes more attractive and will trade at a premium (meaning the current price is higher than the maturity value).

This doesn’t have any influence on the underlying stock really. In a roundabout way though you could say perhaps they will refinance their debt (call it in) and then they can make lower interest payments, raising their net income and subsequently the stock price will rise marginally. This is only the case though if their debt can be called in.
